summary: Richardson Romanesque granite light at Newport Neck, first lit 1 May 1890; the keeper's dwelling was lost in the 1938 hurricane; automated 1957; still active.

structures.note: Rusticated granite conical tower; design possibly by H. H. Richardson (not signed). USLHS: 35 ft from base to center of lantern.
Separate six-room keeper's dwelling, wharf and boathouse about 300 yards east on Castle Hill Cove; destroyed by the 1938 hurricane. Material not stated in the nomination.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination says the fog bell was removed two years after 1890, after Agassiz's complaints about noise; the Board's report dates the discontinuance to 30 November 1891. The story gives both.
USLHS gives 40 ft above water (12.2 m), used here; the NRHP nomination gives 42 ft to the lamp's focal plane. The difference is probably measurement point; not resolved.

The NRHP nomination says the bell was removed two years after 1890 after Agassiz's complaints; the Board's report of 1892 (printed p. 63, scan 412) dates its discontinuance to 30 November 1891. The story gives both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Corrected 2026-10-22 on page images: 1891-92 Castle Hill entry is printed p. 63 (scan 412, 1892 report), not 'scan 402' or a bare scan page; 1896 bell entry (18 March 1896) is printed p. 11 (scan 22), not p. 8 (scan 23); 1897 bell entry is printed p. 57 (scan 310), not scan 311 (corpus scan labels for the 1896-97 volume run one page high); FY1916 table entry is printed p. 57 (scan 166), verified on the page image: Hoxsie is credited with 'Towed disabled launch to Newport'. Bulletin index 1918-1923: the Hexsie entry is on PDF page 16 and refers to Bulletin page 275; year of the efficiency flag not confirmed. Range: the NRHP nomination gives 12 miles (not stated as nautical); the station record's 9.0 nm has no source read; left out of facts. Focal height: USLHS 40 ft above water (used); nomination 42 ft to lamp's focal plane (see resolved_conflicts). NRHP OCR has 'In 1869 a new and more efficient bell' in the fog-bell paragraph, probably a typo; not used. Newspapers: Chronicling America 'Castle Hill' with 'light' (RI, 1889-1940) returned 50 hits, none about the light in the sample read; nothing used. The current optic is 300 mm (USLHS); original fifth order; lens status in the story is not stated. Coast Guard station status now unknown. Johnson's 1889 appropriation ($5,000) in the general corpus; not used. Current status: active aid to navigation per USLHS; NRHP owner and access are from the 1980s nomination and are stated as such in the story. Verification: 2026-10-22 fact-check; nomination text read in full; keeper roster lines copied from the USLHS page. The FY1916 table's 'nature of assistance' column for Hoxsie (Towed disabled launch to Newport) is visible on the page image (scan 166) but not in the OCR text, so it is not stated in the story.
